lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The straw in the drink beside you shows why.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The straw looks snapped because light changes direction when it crosses from water into air.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Air bends light too, because air gets *thicker* the closer it is to the ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So sunlight curves a little as it passes down through each layer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A high Sun's light comes almost straight down, so it barely bends.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But a low Sun's light skims sideways through the thickest air, so it bends the *most*.
